recorded_from_commit_note: This card's rebase of card/144-book-puzzle-frame onto 3c7b7dd (main, after CARD-128 merged as 557c7ac) — the first tree that reproduces these digests, and the tree they were taken from. No earlier commit can: this card's pre-rebase tip (7288f2e) writes an 8-page interior for the same book, because it predates CARD-128's level dividers, and CARD-128's own tree (407c0cc) writes eleven unframed pages. Only the two together produce the eleven pages below. A commit cannot carry its own hash, so this field was filled in by the commit that immediately follows 3350c2a; that commit edits these two fields and nothing else, so it exports the same eleven pages and reproduces them too.
read_back_through: tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages — the pages decoded out of the exported interior PDF, not the in-memory bitmaps
why_a_new_baseline: CARD-144 deliberately changes what a book puzzle page prints, which is the one reason the CARD-145 fixture's warning allows a new baseline to be recorded: FR-041's frame closes the drawing off with one heavy rectangle around clues and grid, so the pages that carry a single puzzle moved. It is recorded against the rebased tree rather than against this card's pre-rebase tip, because CARD-128 merged first and changed the book underneath it: the interior is eleven pages grouped easy/medium/hard with a divider opening each level, not the eight pages the pre-rebase recording described, and the two single-puzzle pages are now interior 5 and interior 7 rather than 2 and 4. Both predecessors are left in place, unregenerated, as the evidence they were recorded to be.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like as of CARD-144. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, which is what G-1 forbids. If a later card deliberately changes a page's content, it records a NEW baseline in a commit of its own, with its own card number, and says so here.
changed_pages_note: The 1-based interior pages whose ink moved against the CARD-128 baseline, and the only ones: interior 5 (the 15x15 Medium) and interior 7 (the 30x30 Hard), the book's two single-puzzle pages, which are now framed. The other nine digests are CARD-128's own, byte for byte. Interior 3 is the two-up page and is identical to the CARD-128 recording, because a two-up page is composed by admin.book_pdf_generator._stroke_drawing, which strokes a slot's grid lines and not its Layout.frame; CARD-144's guardrail G-4 forbade touching that file, so the pair geometry carries a frame per slot that nothing yet draws — tracked as CARD-146 and deliberately out of this card's scope. Interiors 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 are the guide and the four divider pages, which carry no drawing, and 9-11 are the packed answer key, which FR-042 owns and CARD-144 did not touch.
font_fingerprint_note: The guide page and every divider page are lettered in the system's Arial when Pillow can find it and in Pillow's built-in face when it cannot, so those pages' pixels are machine-dependent. A machine whose fingerprint differs from this one cannot be compared against the digests of the pages named in font_dependent_pages. The fingerprint is unchanged from CARD-128's and from CARD-145's: the frame is ink drawn by COMP-007 and touches no lettering, and this is the same machine.
font_dependent_pages_note: The 1-based interior pages whose pixels depend on the machine's own font: page 1 is the guide page (Arial at 48 and 28, load_default fallback), pages 2, 4 and 6 are the Easy, Medium and Hard level dividers and page 8 is the SOLUTIONS divider (Arial at 60). The other six are drawn in the bundled band face and Pillow's built-in clue face, so their digests are comparable on any machine and are compared even when font_fingerprint differs — which is where both of this card's changed pages sit, so the frame's evidence survives a face mismatch. interior_bytes is compared only when the fingerprint matches: those pages sit inside the same file, and a different face changes the length of their JPEG streams.
